cards.explanation: The answer is his sons. Samuel, Israel's leader, appoints his sons as judges over Israel (1 Samuel 8:1). It's the family business, friends. I know that move, because I've handed my stamping to somebody else and watched with my mustache crossed. I think that's a lot to lay on two guys.

The answer is False. The text says Samuel's sons Joel and Abijah “…did not walk in his ways…” (1 Samuel 8:3). They turned aside toward dishonest gain instead. A name on the sign doesn't make the cookies taste the same.

The answer is that they accept bribes and pervert justice. The text says Samuel's sons turned aside toward dishonest gain, “…accepting bribes and perverting justice.” (1 Samuel 8:3) Picture a judge whose ruling goes to the highest bidder. Nobody walks into that courtroom feeling like a winner unless they pay up.

The answer is a king to judge them. The elders say, “Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.” (1 Samuel 8:5) They point to Samuel being old and his sons not walking in his ways. Then comes the big ask, and it's a big one.

The answer is False. When the elders' demand displeased Samuel, the text says “so he prayed to the LORD.” (1 Samuel 8:6) It says nothing about him storming out. When something stings, friends, taking it to the LORD first is a good move.

The answer is the LORD as their king. The LORD says, “For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.” (1 Samuel 8:7) Samuel was the one standing there taking the ask. But the LORD says it was Him they were rejecting. That puts the whole request in a different light.

The answer is True. The LORD says the people have done this “…from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods…” (1 Samuel 8:8) It's a long stretch, and He names it plainly. Then He says they're doing the same thing to Samuel.

The answer is to warn them what their king will be like. The LORD says, “…you must solemnly warn them and show them the manner of the king who will reign over them.” (1 Samuel 8:9) Samuel listens, and then he warns them. It's like reading all the fine print out loud before anyone signs.

The answer is that the king will put them to work for his chariots and horses. Samuel says, “He will take your sons and appoint them to serve his own chariots and horses, and to run in front of his chariots.” (1 Samuel 8:11) Running in front of a chariot is not a job with a comfortable chair. Samuel starts the list there, and it keeps going.

The answer is perfumers and cooks and bakers. Samuel says, “And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.” (1 Samuel 8:13) Bakers made the list, friends, and I felt that one personally. Samuel says “He will take…” so it's the king doing the taking.

The answer is his officials and servants. Samuel says the king “…will take a tenth of your grain and grape harvest and give it to his officials and servants.” (1 Samuel 8:15) Think of a paycheck that gets trimmed before it reaches you. In this case the king's own people get it.

The answer is True, and it's the hardest line of the list. Samuel says, “He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.” (1 Samuel 8:17) The fields, the animals, the harvest, and then the people themselves. Samuel gives the whole picture before they decide.

The answer is False. Samuel says, “…you will beg for relief from the king you have chosen, but the LORD will not answer you on that day.” (1 Samuel 8:18) So the LORD will not answer them on that day. Notice it says the king they have chosen. Samuel says it plainly, and it's a heavy moment.

The answer is that they refuse to listen to Samuel. The text says, “Nevertheless, the people refused to listen to Samuel.” Then they say, “No!” and “We must have a king over us.” (1 Samuel 8:19) Samuel had just read out the full warning. They heard it and still said no.

The answer is that the king will go out before them and fight their battles. The people say they want “…a king to judge us, to go out before us, and to fight our battles.” (1 Samuel 8:20) That's the king they picture, going out before them and fighting. Samuel had just told them what that king will take.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Samuel, “Listen to their voice… Appoint a king for them.” (1 Samuel 8:22) Samuel took every word back to Him, and that's the answer he got. Then Samuel tells the men of Israel to go back to their cities.
